note: Fourth edition (G-79, closing the two gaps its verification named). Two changes of substance over .2, both from a risk-management review. First, the residual can never exceed the inherent band: controls reduce risk, they do not create it, so every residual step is zero or negative and the engine clamps at the inherent band. What used to raise the band now says, in the same words, why nothing was earned back. Second, the inherent band reads the profile rather than the single worst answer: a whole risk area must reach High, or two areas must be elevated. The unit of judgement is the risk area, not any one of the twenty-six answers, so adding questions no longer drags every assessment upward.

two or more risk areas are at High
personal data at High severity in an activity that uses AI
a risk area at High in an activity that is itself High on two or more counts

residual.note: Starts at the inherent band and can only fall. A step is never positive — the engine refuses an edition that tries — because a control cannot make an activity riskier than it is before any control exists. A fall has to be earned by evidence: an assessment that required no control at all has demonstrated nothing and stays where it is. A promised fix is a plan, not a control, and earns nothing until a reviewer settles the finding again to say it is done. The zero steps are the reasons nothing was earned back, and they are shown as such — including the commonest one of all, a control still waiting for a signature, which the second edition left the screen silent about.
